description.narrative: 1.Constituents in Tanzania adopted a Gender responsive National HIV Self Testing (HIV-ST) Framework in July 2020 which also addresses disability issues. 2.Constituents in Tanzania adopted a National Guideline on mainstreaming HIV/AIDS and Non Communicable Diseases (NCDs) interventions in the construction sector in July 2021 with priority given to people living with HIV and AIDS and disability. ILO supported the adoption of the Gender responsive National HIV Self Testing (HIV-ST) Framework by building technical capacity of Trade Union Congress of Tanzania (TUCTA) and Association of Tanzania Employers (ATE) to engage and make strategic contributions into national consultative meetings organised by National AIDS Control Program (NACP) during formulation of the framework. HIV Self-Testing at the Workplace: ILO/WHO Policy Brief, 2018 informed the formulation of The HIVST framework through which world of work elements integrated also targets people with disabilities. In support of the National Guideline on mainstreaming HIV/AIDS and Non Communicable Diseases (NCDs) interventions, in the construction sector 2021, ILO provided financial and normative technical support through technical consultation meetings on the 14 – 15 July 2021 and stakeholder validation meetings on the 19 July 2021. ILO Guidelines on the construction sector and HIV 2008 informed the formulation of the guideline.

Output 6.3. Increased capacity of member States to develop gender-responsive legislation, policies and measures for a world of work free from violence and harassment

description.narrative:
The Association of Tanzania Employers (ATE) , in November 2020, organised a sensitization programme aimed at raising awareness among its members on C190 and R206. Following this sensitization programme, ATE developed and carried out a survey among its affiliates on
the prevalence of violence and harassment and, in particular, of sexual harassment in the world of work; employers' understanding of violence and harassment at work; existing workplace policies to prevent and react to instances of violence and harassment at the workplace. Based on the results of the survey, a report was produced and disseminated in August 2021. Moreover, upon request from its members, ATE agreed upon the following measures to be taken in 2022: (a) carrying out an internal gender; (b) supporting its members in carrying out their own gender audits; (c) supporting the review of internal organisational policies of all ATE's members, with a view to including issues related to violence and harassment. The ILO supported ATE in organising and carrying out the sensitization and training programme in November 2020. Upon request, it also contributed towards the development of the survey and the finalisation of the report.

description.narrative: Trade Union Congress of Tanzania (TUCTA) adopted, in October 2020, a new Gender policy 2021-2026 that aims at promoting equality of opportunity and treatment in leadership between women and men in the trade union leadership. The policy promotes gender equality between women and men in TUCTA in decision-making, staffing and human resources, and organizational culture shall be crucial in implementing the Gender Policy. It also commits the organisation advance gender equality through gender analysis and mainstreaming to be conducted in all technical work, operational activities and support services including knowledge management. Finally, it seeks to strengthen institutional arrangements to promote accountability for mainstreaming gender and mechanisms for mainstreaming gender into programming, implementation, monitoring and evaluation. With the support from ILO, TUCTA conducted a Participatory Gender Audit (PGA) in August 2020, of which one of the key findings was the need to review the 2014 TUCTA's Gender Policy to bring it at par with the current TUCTA's needs and circumstances and to address challenges around the implementation of the gender equality commitments within TUCTA and its affiliates. In addition, the ILO provided substantive technical inputs and guidance through the drafting and the finalisation of the Gender policy and facilitated consultative meetings with Gender Focal Point from 10 main TUCTA affiliates.
